backlog.spec: Replace construct_packing with: start from the two-ring layout, then run scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) on variables [x,y,r] (78 vars), objective -sum(r), vectorised inequality constraints: pairwise (dx^2+dy^2 - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0 or dist - ri - rj >= 0) for all i<j, and r<=x<=1-r, r<=y<=1-r, r>=0. Supply analytic jacobians. maxiter 500. At the end shrink radii by 1e-12 and recompute a safe radii via pairwise check. Return centers, radii.
backlog.title: SLSQP joint optimisation of centers and radii

backlog.spec: Seeded (np.random.default_rng(0)) multi-start: for each of many random uniform center sets (about 30-60 within time budget of ~200s), compute LP radii, then refine with SLSQP on (x,y,r). Keep the best valid packing. Track time.time() and stop at 200s.
backlog.title: Multi-start SLSQP with random centers

backlog.spec: Given centers, solve radii exactly via scipy.optimize.linprog (max sum r s.t. r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=border distance). Outer loop: basin hopping—perturb a few centers with Gaussian noise sigma 0.02-0.05, re-solve LP, accept if better (or with Metropolis). Finish with SLSQP polish of best.
backlog.title: LP radii inner solve with outer centre perturbation

backlog.spec: Initialise centers from a hexagonal lattice (rows of 5/6 alternating, e.g. 5-6-5-6-4 variants) with jitter, trimmed to 26 points; run LP+SLSQP. Try several row patterns and lattice offsets and pick the best.
backlog.title: Hex-grid-like initialisations with removal

backlog.spec: Start from a 5x5 grid of equal circles plus one extra circle placed in a gap, with small random jitter; optimise with SLSQP over centers and radii. Try many seeds of jitter and keep the best.
backlog.title: Square-grid 5x5 plus one init

backlog.spec: Stage 1: minimise -sum(r) + mu*sum(overlap^2) + wall violation^2 using L-BFGS-B over (x,y,r) with mu increasing 10,100,1e3,1e4,1e5. Stage 2: SLSQP polish with hard constraints. Multiple random starts, seeded.
backlog.title: Penalty-method gradient descent then SLSQP

backlog.spec: Simulate repulsion: circles with target radii growing; each step push overlapping circles apart along the center line and clamp against walls, with step size decaying. After convergence, LP radii and SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Annealed radius-growth physics simulation

backlog.spec: Initialise 4 large circles (r~0.13) at the corners, edge circles of medium size along the sides, and smaller circles in the interior with random positions; then SLSQP. Randomise sizes across seeds.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored large circles init

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii that decrease with distance from the center in a random Poisson-like layout (rejection sampling with radius-dependent spacing), then run SLSQP jointly on centers and radii.
backlog.title: Size-graded init: big center, small edges

backlog.spec: Use scipy trust-constr with sparse Jacobians for the same constrained problem, starting from the best SLSQP solution of a quick multi-start, to see whether it finds different local optima.
backlog.title: Trust-constr alternative

backlog.spec: From the incumbent best optimum, repeatedly: pick the smallest 1-3 circles, relocate them to random positions (or biggest holes via sampled points maximizing distance to others), re-run SLSQP for ~100 iterations, accept if better. Run until 200s.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-reoptimise iterated local search

backlog.spec: In iterated local search, add a move that swaps the positions of two circles with very different radii, then re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept improvements only.
backlog.title: Swap-radii moves

backlog.spec: Start from random points, apply 20 Lloyd iterations (estimated using a dense grid sample of the square) to get an even spread, then LP radii and SLSQP. Seeds loop.
backlog.title: Voronoi/Lloyd-relaxed initial centers

backlog.spec: Optimise a packing with 27 circles via SLSQP, then delete the circle with the smallest radius, re-optimise with 26. Also try from 28 deleting two. Pick the best.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert from 27/28 circle packing

backlog.spec: Impose mirror symmetry about the diagonal (or x=0.5): optimise 13-ish free circles plus on-axis circles, with mirrored copies. Reduced dimension searches faster; then release the symmetry and polish with full SLSQP.
backlog.title: Symmetric-constrained search

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, refine using a barrier method: minimise -sum r - t*sum(log(slack)) with decreasing t using L-BFGS or Newton steps, keeping strictly feasible; yields robust validity and sometimes tighter optimum.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior point refinement

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, identify the active constraints (slack<1e-9), and solve the KKT/equality system with Newton's method (np.linalg.lstsq) to tighten to machine precision, then shrink radii by 1e-13.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish

backlog.spec: Final post-processing: compute radii = min(r, wall distance), then iteratively for each violating pair shrink both by the overlap/2 + 1e-12 until no violations in double precision; verify with an explicit check. Minimises loss of sum while guaranteeing validity.
backlog.title: Safe final radii fix-up

backlog.spec: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution over 52 center coordinates with a fitness equal to minus the LP-optimal sum of radii (linprog highs), small popsize, seeded, limited to ~150s, then SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Differential evolution on centers with LP inner

backlog.spec: Parametrise as rows of circles (counts like 4,5,6,5,6 or 5,5,6,5,5) with free x per circle and free y per row; run LP+SLSQP over many row-count compositions summing to 26 and pick the best.
backlog.title: Row-structured parametrisation

backlog.spec: First optimise maximise sum r^p with p growing from 2 down to 1 via SLSQP warm starts (p=2 encourages equality, then p=1 allows size variance), final stage p=1.
backlog.title: Staged radii-power objective

backlog.spec: Within SLSQP, include only pair constraints for pairs whose distance is below 0.4 at the start; recheck and re-add violated pairs, looping. Speeds iterations so more restarts fit in the time budget.
backlog.title: Constraint subset for speed

backlog.spec: From the best solution, multiply the radii of random circles by U(0.7,1.3) and move centers by Gaussian 0.01, run SLSQP, repeat; adaptively accept with simulated annealing temperature decreasing 1e-3 to 1e-5.
backlog.title: Random-radius-ratio perturbation of optimum

backlog.spec: Place 12 circles around the perimeter (3 per side including corners, equally spaced), a ring of 8 inside, and 6 in the center region, with jitter; optimise via SLSQP. Vary ring counts (e.g. 12/8/6, 14/8/4, 10/10/6).
backlog.title: Edge-heavy ring init

backlog.spec: Build incrementally: add circles one at a time, each placed at the point of a fine grid maximising the inscribed circle radius amid the existing ones, with random tie-breaking of sizes; after every few additions run SLSQP on the current set. Several seeds.
backlog.title: Hole-filling greedy construction

backlog.spec: Maintain a population of 8 solutions; each round, optimise by SLSQP after perturbation with differing noise levels, then replace the worst with a copy of the best plus perturbation. Time-limited to 200s with fixed seed.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering-like population

backlog.spec: Formulate pair constraints as (xi-xj)^2+(yi-yj)^2-(ri+rj)^2>=0 with vectorised analytic Jacobian built with np.triu_indices; this improves SLSQP speed and smoothness compared with sqrt forms, enabling more restarts.
backlog.title: Use squared-distance constraints with analytic Jacobian

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP with ftol=1e-14 and maxiter=2000 for the final polish of the top 3 candidates from the multi-start, picking the best after validity repair.
backlog.title: Tight tolerance SLSQP, ftol 1e-15

backlog.spec: Use scipy.optimize.basinhopping with SLSQP as the local minimiser (constraints passed in minimizer_kwargs), a custom take_step that jiggles centers by 0.03 and sets radii to the LP-feasible values, niter limited by time, seed fixed.
backlog.title: Basin-hopping with scipy.optimize.basinhopping

backlog.spec: After the multi-start loop (reserve about 60s of the 150s budget), run iterated local search from the best packing. Each iteration: copy best centers, pick the 1-3 circles with smallest radii, move them to random positions (or to the largest empty hole found by evaluating the max distance-to-nearest-circle/wall on the grid _GRID), add Gaussian noise of sigma 0.01 to all centers, run _lp_radii then _polish then _lp_radii. Accept if the sum improves (or with small Metropolis probability). Keep the best. Finish with the existing 1e-10 shrink.
backlog.title: Basin-hopping from incumbent: relocate smallest circles

backlog.spec: For half of the starts, generate init centers with a symmetry: sample 13 points, reflect across the diagonal x<->y (points on the diagonal count once, so mix e.g. 4 diagonal points plus 11 pairs = 26). Run Lloyd and the polish on the full 26 circle problem without enforcing symmetry afterwards. Symmetric starts reach different basins. Keep the best by sum of radii over all starts.
backlog.title: Symmetric-constrained search (mirror/diagonal)

backlog.spec: Add a start generator: pick a hex lattice with random row count (5 or 6), random orientation (rows along x or y), random spacing 0.17-0.2, random shift. Take all lattice points inside [0.05,0.95]^2, and if more than 26 remove random ones; if fewer add random points. Add jitter sigma 0.005, then use _lp_radii and _polish. Use it for 30% of the starts.
backlog.title: Hex-grid init with random row offsets and deletions

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform-density Lloyd with a weighted Lloyd: the grid sample density is w(p)=1+a*dist-to-center-of-square-based term, so that cells near the center are larger. Draw a randomly from [-1,2] per start. This yields initial centers with large circles in the middle and small near the edges, or the reverse. Then LP radii and SLSQP polish as usual.
backlog.title: Size-graded init with weighted Lloyd

backlog.spec: For each start, draw target radii r_i from a lognormal distribution (sigma 0.3) scaled so the sum is about 2.6. Run 30 iterations of a repulsion relaxation: for overlapping pairs (dist<r_i+r_j) push centers apart proportionally to the overlap, and push centers inside the walls so x in [r,1-r]. Use the result as the start for the LP and the polish. This is a different physical init from Lloyd.
backlog.title: Power-diagram init from random radii

backlog.spec: Within _polish, include only pair constraints with initial center distance below 0.45 (about 3x typical radius sum) instead of all 325 pairs. This makes each SLSQP run several times faster and allows about 3x more starts in the time budget. After polishing, verify with the full _lp_radii, which keeps validity. Use the saved time for more starts.
backlog.title: Polish with a shrinking-active-set filtered constraint list

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, take the top 5 distinct packings. For each, run 20 kicks: multiply the radii of 4 random circles by 0.7-1.3, set x0 to the current centers with those radii, and run SLSQP via _polish modified to accept the starting radii. Then _lp_radii. Keep any improvement. This explores the neighbouring contact-graph changes of the incumbent.
backlog.title: Perturb radii ratios then re-polish (kick of radius vector)

backlog.spec: Before _polish, run scipy L-BFGS-B on variables (x,y,r) minimising -sum r + mu*(sum of squared pair overlap violations + sum of squared wall violations), with mu stepped through 10, 100, 1000, 10000, using analytic gradients with numpy vectorization. Then SLSQP polish from that point. The soft stage lets circles slide through jammed states which SLSQP alone can't.
backlog.title: Penalty-based soft optimisation with L-BFGS before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Take the best packing found and its contact graph. Use the null-space of the active-constraint Jacobian (SVD) to generate random feasible moves: add a random combination of the smallest-singular-vector directions with step size 0.02, then re-run _polish. Repeat as a local search for 40s. This is a bolder move than random noise and keeps the packing near-feasible.
backlog.title: Differential evolution of the best packing in a low-dimensional subspace

backlog.spec: Take the best packing. For each circle k (26 loop), remove it, find the point maximizing the distance to the others' circle boundaries and walls (grid search on _GRID using current radii), put the circle there, run _polish and _lp_radii. Accept if the sum improves, then repeat the pass with the new best. Do this as the final phase for about 40s of budget.
backlog.title: Remove-one and reinsert at the largest hole

backlog.spec: After the multi-start loop (reduce its budget to ~90s), run an iterated local search from the best packing for the remaining ~60s. Each move: pick k=1-3 circles (biased to the smallest radii), move each to a random location (or the largest empty point from a dense grid distance map), add small gaussian jitter (sigma 0.01) to all centers, then run _lp_radii and _polish. Accept if the sum improves, or with a small Metropolis probability (T~0.002). Keep the best seen. Use the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Basin-hopping: relocate smallest circles

backlog.spec: From the incumbent best packing, repeatedly remove one random circle (prefer small), compute the largest empty circle location on a 200x200 grid using distance to the remaining circle surfaces and the walls, place the circle there with radius 0, then run _polish with the other circles slightly shrunk. Accept improvements only. Loop until the time limit, with about 60s reserved after the multi-start.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert at largest hole

backlog.spec: For the top 5 distinct packings found, apply perturbation to the radii: multiply the radii by lognormal noise (sigma 0.15), then shrink the centers' mutual distances to be feasible by calling _polish with starting x0 from the perturbed radii and nudged centers (move centers by a small step along gradients of the overlaps). Re-polish with SLSQP and keep the best. Repeat over many kicks within a time budget.
backlog.title: Radius-vector kick then re-polish

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, optimize x=[centers, radii] with L-BFGS-B on the objective -sum(r) + mu*(sum of squared pair overlaps + squared wall violations), with mu rising geometrically 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5. Use analytic gradients with vectorised numpy. Start from the Lloyd, hex, and random initialisations. This is cheaper than SLSQP, so it allows 5-10x more starts. SLSQP then polishes only the best 20% by penalty value.
backlog.title: Soft penalty L-BFGS pre-stage with annealed exponent

backlog.spec: Run many more starts (say 1000) by doing a short SLSQP polish (maxiter 40) on each. Rank by the LP radii sum. Then fully polish (maxiter 300) only the top 10 and return the best. This is a batching change to spend the time budget on breadth.
backlog.title: Two-phase screen: cheap rank then polish top candidates

backlog.spec: Draw random radii from a bimodal distribution (a few large 0.14, many 0.08-0.10). Sample centers by running weighted Lloyd with a power distance d^2 - r^2 on the dense grid, 20 iterations. Use the resulting centers and radii as the SLSQP start. Mix it in at about 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Power-diagram initialisation from random radii

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that places a 5x5 square grid of centers (spacing 0.2) and adds a 26th circle at a random interstitial position. Apply random shear and rotation of 0-15 degrees to the grid, jitter by sigma 0.02, and clip. Mix in at about 15% of starts.
backlog.title: Perturbed-lattice init with a 5x5 grid plus one

backlog.spec: Take the best packing. Define the subspace as the centers of the 6 smallest circles (12 dims). Run scipy differential_evolution (popsize 10, maxiter 30, seeded) with an objective of -LP radii sum of the centers, bounds are ±0.15 around the current positions clipped to [0,1]. Polish the best DE result with _polish. Accept if better.
backlog.title: Differential evolution in low-dim subspace

backlog.spec: For the top 3 packings, run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same [x,y,r] vector, using the analytic constraint Jacobian (sparse where possible) and the same bounds. Use a BFGS or SR1 Hessian with xtol 1e-12, maxiter 1000. Then a final LP. Keep it if it beats SLSQP; this may escape SLSQP's stopping points.
backlog.title: Trust-constr alternative polish

backlog.spec: Replace the final r - 1e-10 with an exact feasibility repair. Compute, in double precision, for each pair the violation r_i+r_j-d and for walls the violation, then do a loop that subtracts the violation/2 plus 1e-15 from the offending radii until none remain. Re-run the LP on the final centers with the pair rhs d*(1-1e-13) and wall bounds reduced by 1e-13, in order to recover about 1e-10 of sum. Verify with a checker and fall back to the old shrink if verification fails.
backlog.title: Safe radius fix-up with exact margin

backlog.spec: Change nothing in the search logic except confirming determinism: keep seed 12345 and the 150s loop, but replace the time-based loop termination with a fixed iteration count (for example 220 starts, tuned so it finishes in about 150s) so results do not depend on machine speed. Final radii shrink stays at 1e-10. This checks repeatability and removes clock-dependent variance.
backlog.title: Replicate run for repeatability

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, recompute radii with a LP using centers, then run a verification pass in double precision. For every violating pair, shrink both radii by the overlap amount. For every wall violation, clip the radius to the wall distance. Then subtract only 1e-13 instead of 1e-10. The gain is about 2.6e-9, which is tiny but safe, and a final validity check guards it.
backlog.title: Exact-margin final radius fix-up

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that draws 26 random radii from a lognormal (sigma 0.4), then runs Lloyd iterations on the dense grid using power distance (d^2 - r^2) for assignment. Centroids of the power cells become the centers, with small jitter. Use it for about 30% of starts so the initial layouts have mixed circle sizes.
backlog.title: Power-diagram init from random radii

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run L-BFGS-B on x=[X,Y,R] minimising -sum(R) + mu*sum(max(0, overlap)^2) over pair and wall violations. Anneal mu through 10, 100, 1000, 1e4 with analytic gradients. Pass the result to the existing SLSQP polish. This gives SLSQP a smoother start than raw inits and may reach different basins.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty L-BFGS pre-stage

backlog.spec: Run a cheap SLSQP with maxiter=40 on each start, then rank all starts by LP sum. Spend the full 300-iteration polish only on the top 15%. This gives about 3-4x more starts in the same time budget. Implement it as a generate-and-screen phase for 100s, then a full polish of the top K for 50s.
backlog.title: Two-phase screening

backlog.spec: After the multi-start (shortened to 100s), run an iterated local search from the best packing. Each move picks two circles with different radii and swaps their centers, or moves the smallest circle to a random point. Then run an SLSQP polish with maxiter=100. Accept the move if the LP sum improves. Use a swap move because it changes the topology of which sizes sit where. Run it until 145s.
backlog.title: Swap-radii and relocation moves from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Generate initial centers by sampling 26 points where the density is high near the square edges and corners (for example, push uniform points outward by x -> 0.5 + 0.5*sign*|2x-1|^0.7). Set the initial radii to be 0.14 at the center and 0.06 at the edges, and pass these radii to SLSQP as x0 instead of the LP radii. Use it for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Size-graded init with big center, small edges

backlog.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct candidates from the multi-start. Re-optimise each with scipy trust-constr (using the analytic Jacobian and a BFGS Hessian, 400 iterations). Run the LP on each result, and take the best one if it beats the SLSQP result. The different algorithm may escape SLSQP's tolerance stalls.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish on the top candidates

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that places a 5x5 square grid with spacing 0.2, with a random jitter of 0.02, plus one extra circle in a random gap, with the number of circles per row varying by one. Run SLSQP with random radii scaling. This is a different topology from the hex-based starts, and the best known structures for n=26 look partly grid-like at the corners.
backlog.title: Perturbed 5x5 grid plus one

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, take the best packing and run scipy differential_evolution (seed fixed, popsize 15, 25s budget) over a 10-dimensional vector: shifts of the 5 smallest circles' centers within ±0.08 of their current positions. The fitness is the LP radii sum. Then polish the best DE result with SLSQP. This is a global search in a small subspace.
backlog.title: Differential evolution with LP inner, low dimension

backlog.spec: Make a harmless change: keep the search as is, but change the final margin from r - 1e-10 to a computed exact margin. After the final LP, compute max pairwise overlap (r_i + r_j - d_ij) and wall violation in double precision, then subtract only that violation plus 1e-15 from the affected radii. This confirms validity and the repeatability of -2.6360 while recovering about 1e-10.
backlog.title: Replicate run for repeatability

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, take the best packing and extract its contact graph (pairs with gap < 1e-7). Generate neighbours by removing one contact edge: push the two circles apart along the line of centres by 0.02, shrink both radii by 30%, and re-polish with SLSQP. Also try flipping a rattler circle to another hole. Accept if the sum improves. Run for about 60s after a 90s multi-start.
backlog.title: Contact-graph topology moves

backlog.spec: Draw random radii from a lognormal or from a graded distribution (larger near the center). Build a weighted (power) Lloyd iteration on the dense grid. Each grid point is assigned to the circle minimising |p-c|^2 - r^2. Move centres to the cell centroids for 20 iterations. Use the result as an SLSQP init, as a new generator alongside the existing ones with about 25% weight.
backlog.title: Power-diagram init from random radii

backlog.spec: Phase 1: run many cheap starts with SLSQP maxiter=40 for 70s and keep the top 10 by LP radii sum. Phase 2: fully polish only those 10 with maxiter=300 and ftol=1e-12 for 60s, then choose the best. This gives more starts per unit time and ranks them cheaply.
backlog.title: Two-phase screening of starts

backlog.spec: From the best packing, apply moves. Swap the positions of two circles with very different radii and re-polish. Or exchange a large circle with its smaller neighbour. Run SLSQP with a start radius of min(r_i, r_j) for the swapped pair. Run these moves for 60s after a 90s multi-start. Accept improvements only.
backlog.title: Radius-swap and relocation moves

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 packings from the multi-start. Re-polish each with scipy trust-constr (using the same analytic Jacobian for the squared-distance constraints, BFGS Hessian or SR1), maxiter 500. This may reach a different local optimum than SLSQP. Finish with the LP radii.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the top candidates

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise with L-BFGS-B over (x,y,r) the objective -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2 + wall violation^2). Use mu from 10 to 1e4 in 5 stages, starting from random centres and small radii. Run it for hundreds of cheap starts and polish only the best 20% with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty annealed pre-stage with random radii targets

backlog.spec: Polish the best packing with a regularised objective: maximise sum r - lam*sum (r_i - rbar)^2 for lam in {0.5, 0.2, 0.05, 0}, one SLSQP stage each. This pushes the packing toward more uniform radii first, then relaxes it, giving different basins. Run on the top 5 multi-start candidates, and keep the best final sum.
backlog.title: Radius-ratio kick with penalty regularization

backlog.spec: Optimise 13 mirror-pair circles under a 180-degree rotational symmetry (centre (0.5,0.5), c -> 1-c). Use SLSQP on half the variables for 60s of random starts. Then unfreeze to all 26 circles and re-polish the top 5. Symmetric starts halve the dimension and may find structured optima that a general search misses.
backlog.title: Symmetric-constrained subspace search with unfreezing

backlog.spec: Leave the search unchanged. Replace the final `r = np.maximum(r - 1e-10, 0)` with a safe fix-up: compute the max pairwise overlap and wall violation in double precision, then shrink each radius by min(1e-13, ...) just enough so that all checks r_i+r_j<=d_ij and r_i<=min(x,y,1-x,1-y) hold exactly. Verify with an explicit loop and shrink again by 1e-15 if any check fails. Reduce the margin from 1e-10 to roughly 1e-14 to gain about 2.6e-9. Also doubles as a repeatability check.
backlog.title: Replicate run with exact-margin radius fix-up

backlog.spec: Run the multi-start as now, keeping the top 4 distinct (by sum) polished packings. For each, run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' on [x,y,r] with the same squared-distance constraints as a NonlinearConstraint with analytic Jacobian and a BFGS or SR1 Hessian, gtol=1e-12, maxiter 500. Finish with the LP radii solve and keep the best valid result. Limit the multi-start to 120s to leave time.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of top candidates

backlog.spec: After a 100s multi-start, take the best packing and find its contact graph (pairs with gap <1e-7). Spend about 90s on topology moves. Pick a circle with a low contact count or small radius and delete it. Insert it at a random point of the largest empty hole, found by grid sampling of the distance to the nearest circle or wall. Alternatively, swap the positions of two circles with different radii. Then run SLSQP polish with maxiter 150 and accept if the sum improves. Use the fixed seed.
backlog.title: Contact-graph topology moves

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that builds a packing incrementally. Start with 4 random circles. Repeatedly find the point on a 200x200 grid with the largest distance to the existing circles' boundaries and walls (with some randomness, e.g. pick among the top 5). Add a circle there with that radius times 0.9. Continue to 26 circles. Then do the SLSQP polish. Give this initialiser about 30% of the starts.
backlog.title: Hole-filling greedy construction

backlog.spec: For about 40s of the budget, optimise under a symmetry. Use a diagonal mirror (x,y)->(y,x). Parametrise 13 free circles, or k on-axis circles plus mirror pairs, and mirror them. Run SLSQP on the reduced variables with the full constraint set. Take the best few symmetric solutions as initial points and run the unconstrained full SLSQP polish, which breaks the symmetry. Keep the best overall.
backlog.title: Symmetric-subspace search with unfreezing

backlog.spec: Polish in two stages. Stage 1 maximises sum r_i + lambda*sum log(r_i+1e-3) with lambda=0.02 using SLSQP, which discourages tiny circles and changes the basin. Stage 2 drops the log term and maximises sum r. Run on all starts. This is a regularisation of the objective, unlike the earlier power-objective stage, because it uses a log barrier on small radii.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective homotopy

backlog.spec: Use a larger batch of starts, aiming at about 3x more. For each start, run SLSQP with maxiter=60 using only the neighbour pairs (distance <0.35). Rank by the LP radii sum on the full constraints. Fully polish only the top 8% with the complete constraint set and maxiter 300. Keep the best.
backlog.title: Cheap-screen with many more starts via fewer constraints

backlog.spec: Spend 60s on this after the multi-start. Take the best 3 packings. For each trial, multiply the centers' deviations from the packing centroid by a scale factor in [0.97,1.03]. Add Gaussian jitter of sigma in [0.005,0.03] to 3-6 random circles only. Re-polish with SLSQP. Accept if better and keep a pool of the best 3.
backlog.title: Perturbed incumbent-topology restarts with radius-ratio jitter

backlog.spec: Make a structured initialiser. Place 4 circles near the corners with radius about 0.13. Put 6 circles along the edge midpoints with radius about 0.11. Arrange the remaining 16 in a staggered interior grid of rows 4-4-4-4 with random jitter. Randomly choose which of 2-3 template variants to use, and randomly assign radii. Polish with SLSQP. Use this for 25% of the starts.
backlog.title: Square-corner big circles with a 3-row interior template

backlog.spec: Run SA for about 80s starting from the best packing. The state is the centers. The energy is minus the LP-optimal radii sum. Each move perturbs 1-2 random circles with Gaussian sigma about 0.02, decreasing with the temperature. The temperature goes from 0.005 to 1e-5 geometrically. After the annealing, polish the best state with SLSQP. Seed the RNG for repeatability.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing on centers with LP objective

backlog.spec: Keep the search unchanged. Replace the final `r = np.maximum(r - 1e-10, 0)` with an exact check in double precision: compute all pairwise gaps d_ij - r_i - r_j and wall slacks min(x-r, 1-x-r, y-r, 1-y-r). If any is negative, shrink the offending radii by that amount plus 1e-15. Otherwise shrink only by 1e-13. Also set the sum to float64 np.sum(r). This checks repeatability and recovers about 1e-10 of margin.
backlog.title: Replicate run with exact-margin radius fix-up

backlog.spec: Use 4 independent RNG seeds (12345, 1, 2, 3) in round-robin, each with its own best-so-far. Give each ~40s. Then spend the last 30s re-polishing the best of each with SLSQP at maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-15. This diversifies the starts beyond the single sequence.
backlog.title: Interleaved multi-seed schedule

backlog.spec: After a 110s multi-start, find rattlers (circles with fewer than 3 contacts) and the smallest-radius circles. Remove them and re-place them at random points inside the 5 largest holes, with fresh radii, then polish. Also try 2-for-1 swaps: replace two small adjacent circles by one at their midpoint, plus one new circle at the biggest hole. Accept improvements only.
backlog.title: Rattler-aware relocation search

backlog.spec: Change the rng seed in optimized_packing from 12345 to 777 and keep everything else the same, to measure seed variance of the plateau at -2.6360 and check whether the incumbent is a lucky or robust basin. Report the result as-is.
backlog.title: Replicate run with seed change

backlog.spec: Split the 150s budget into 5 equal windows, each with a fresh default_rng(seed_k) for seeds 1..5, and keep the global best. This diversifies the search against a single RNG stream getting stuck in one family of initialisations.
backlog.title: Multi-seed interleaved restarts

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, take the best packing and identify active constraints (gaps below 1e-7 for pairs and walls). Solve the square system of active equalities for (x,y,r) by Gauss-Newton with lstsq, with r added by LP-dual-guided selection. Accept the result only if the LP radii sum on the result improves by more than 1e-12. The goal is to remove the residual SLSQP tolerance error.
backlog.title: Fixed-contact-graph Newton solve

backlog.spec: Spend 50s of the budget finding the best 25-circle packings using the same pipeline with n=25 (parametrise n). For the top 5, insert a 26th circle at each of the 8 largest-clearance holes (found on a grid with the radius as the clearance). Then run SLSQP and LP on the 26 circles, and compare with the incumbent from the remaining 100s of the standard multi-start.
backlog.title: Grow from 25-circle optimum

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that places 4 circles in the corners with radius about 0.13, 4 mid-edge circles at the wall, and the other 18 circles on a jittered 3-row interior hex pattern. Use it for 30% of starts, then the usual SLSQP polish. This tests the corner and edge structure with large circles that the best known packings seem to use.
backlog.title: Corner-big-circle template

backlog.spec: Run each start for 40 SLSQP iterations with only the pairs within 0.3 distance. Abandon starts whose LP sum is below 2.55. Fully polish only starts above that with the full constraint set. This raises the number of starts for the same time by about 3x.
backlog.title: Larger cheap batch with early abandonment

backlog.spec: From the best packing, pick a random active pair constraint and temporarily push the two circles apart by 0.02. Shrink their radii by 30% and re-polish with SLSQP. Accept if better. Repeat for about 60s. This explicitly changes the contact topology, unlike random center jitter.
backlog.title: Contact-graph constraint removal perturbation

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run L-BFGS-B on x,y,r with objective -sum r + mu * sum max(0, overlap)^2 over the pairs and walls. Use mu in [10, 100, 1e3, 1e4], analytic gradients, and radii initialised to 0.05. This gives smoother basin selection than direct SLSQP from random starts. Use it for 40% of starts.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty annealed pre-stage with power exponent

backlog.spec: Replace the single default_rng(12345) multi-start with 6 independent generators (seeds 1..6) used round-robin inside the existing 150s loop, so each seed gets a different start stream. Keep the global best. Purpose: diversify the start distribution and check whether the 2.6360 plateau is seed-dependent. Keep the 1e-10 final shrink.
backlog.title: Rotating-seed interleaved multi-start

backlog.spec: Spend the first 40s optimising 25-circle packings with the same SLSQP machinery (N=25, own LP routine). Take the best 5. For each, insert a 26th circle at the largest empty point (grid search of the max clearance), start it with a small radius, run full 26-circle SLSQP. Merge into the candidate pool, then continue the normal multi-start for the remaining time.
backlog.title: Grow from the 25-circle optimum

backlog.spec: For about half of the starts, first run SLSQP (maxiter 80) maximising sum w_i r_i with w_i drawn from Uniform(0.5,1.5), then run the standard unweighted polish from that result. The weights push the topology toward different big/small circle assignments before the true objective takes over.
backlog.title: Random weighted-objective homotopy

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 distinct packings from a 120s multi-start. Refine each with scipy trust-constr using the same constraints, analytic Jacobians, and BFGS or sr1 Hessian. Use gtol 1e-12 and maxiter 500. Rerun the LP on the result and take the best across all candidates and the original.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the top candidates

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that builds a lattice with basis vectors a=s(cos t, sin t) and b=s(cos(t+phi), sin(t+phi)), s in [0.17,0.21], t random, phi in [55,90] degrees, random offset. Keep the points inside [0.04,0.96]^2 and snap points within 0.06 of a wall to the wall at distance 0.08. Randomly drop or add points to reach 26. Use it for 30% of starts.
backlog.title: Sheared rotated lattice initialiser

backlog.spec: After a 100s multi-start, loop for 50s. In each pass, take the best packing. Pick a random circle pair in contact and push the two apart by 0.03 along their line, or pick a random circle and move it 0.05 in a random direction. Reduce all radii by 20% and re-run SLSQP, then the LP. Accept only if the sum improves.
backlog.title: Contact-graph removal perturbation

backlog.spec: Run SLSQP in chunks of 40 iterations using warm-start continuation. After the first chunk, compute the LP sum for the point. Abandon the start if the sum is below 2.55. Continue the rest to full convergence. Because most starts are dropped early, this gives roughly 3x more starts in the same 150s. Keep the existing initialiser mix.
backlog.title: Bigger cheap-start batch with early abandonment

backlog.spec: Make no functional change to train.py except changing nothing in the search; simply rerun to confirm repeatability of the -2.6360 incumbent (fixed seed 12345, time-based loop end at 150s). To make it deterministic, replace the wall-clock loop condition with a fixed iteration count (e.g. 400 starts) wrapped with a time guard of 200s as a backstop, and report the result.
backlog.title: Replicate run, unchanged

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, take the best packing, identify active constraints (pair gaps < 1e-9 and wall gaps < 1e-9), and solve the square system of active equalities for (x,y,r) with Newton/least-squares (scipy.optimize.least_squares, method 'lm') starting from the best solution. Accept only if the resulting radii pass exact double-precision checks and sum increases. Then apply the 1e-10 shrink.
backlog.title: Fixed contact-graph Newton solve

backlog.spec: For each start, run SLSQP first with objective sum w_i r_i where w_i ~ uniform(0.5,1.5) for 80 iterations, then with w interpolated linearly to 1 over 3 stages, with final full-weight polish. This diversifies the basins reached. Use for 50% of starts.
backlog.title: Random weighted-objective homotopy

backlog.spec: Use 4 independent RNG streams seeded 12345, 1, 2, 3 and rotate between them each start, tracking each one's best. At the end, re-polish the top candidate of each stream with SLSQP ftol 1e-14 and return the best overall. Total budget stays at 150s.
backlog.title: Interleaved multi-seed restarts

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser generating a lattice with random basis vectors (spacing 0.17-0.21, random rotation, shear up to 0.3), take points inside [0.05,0.95]^2, snap those within 0.08 of a wall onto distance 0.08 from the wall, then randomly delete or add circles to reach 26. Use for 30% of starts.
backlog.title: Sheared rotated lattice init

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run L-BFGS-B on x,y,r variables maximising sum r minus mu*sum of squared overlap violations (pair and wall), with analytic gradients, annealing mu through 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4. Initial radii are lognormal(0.4)-distributed with sum scaled to 2.3. Feed the result to SLSQP. Use on 50% of starts.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty annealed pre-stage with power exponent

backlog.spec: Make no edits to train.py except a trivial comment change, so the same seed 12345 runs again. This checks that -2.6360 is repeatable and that the result does not depend on wall-clock effects, since the loop stops on a time limit. Report the official loss.
backlog.title: Replicate run unchanged

backlog.spec: Replace the time-based loop `while time.time()-t0<150` with a fixed number of starts, calibrated to roughly 200s on this machine, for example by timing the first 5 starts and extrapolating once. Keep a hard time cap of 220s as a safety limit. This makes the result deterministic and lets the whole budget be used, with the final polish and checks done afterwards.
backlog.title: Iteration-count-limited multistart

backlog.spec: After the best centers are chosen, solve the LP for radii once more. Then compute the double-precision worst violation of every pair and wall constraint and scale all radii by the single factor (1 - max_violation_ratio - 1e-15), instead of subtracting a fixed 1e-10 from each radius. Check that the result is valid with exact arithmetic. This gains about 2.6e-9 at most, so it is a safe small gain.
backlog.title: Tighter exact-feasibility radius scaling

backlog.spec: Take the best packing and identify the active constraints with slack below 1e-9. Solve the KKT system for the sum-of-radii objective by Newton's method with the multipliers as unknowns, using lstsq. Accept the result only if the LP-checked sum improves. This corrects the residual 1e-9 error left by SLSQP.
backlog.title: Second-order active-set final solve with KKT multipliers

backlog.spec: Initialise the start with three size classes of circles: 4 large circles near the corners, 12 medium circles at the edges and 10 small circles inside. Give each class a random target radius and place the circles by sequential dart throwing with those radii. Run the SLSQP polish with the target radii as the starting r. Use this for 25% of the starts.
backlog.title: Cluster-pair symmetric lattice start with 3 radius classes

backlog.spec: Polish each start with SLSQP on an objective that is the negative sum of r_i, plus a small random linear weight w_i*r_i with w_i drawn from N(0,0.05). Then drop the weights and polish again. Use the perturbed objective to reach different contact graphs. Apply it to the top 10 starts only, with a different random weight each time.
backlog.title: Objective smoothing via p-norm continuation on radii

backlog.spec: From the best packing, pick a random disc of radius 0.25 in the square. Re-randomise the centers of all circles inside it, with radii reset to half. Freeze the other circles' centers for a first SLSQP run with bounds of ±0.02, then free everything and polish again. Repeat for about 60s and accept an improvement only.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood search by re-solving a sub-region

backlog.spec: Generate starts from a grid of rows with counts drawn from compositions of 26 into 5 or 6 rows. Stretch each row's x-spacing so that the row fills the width. Add a random vertical sinusoidal wave of amplitude 0.03 to each row, and swap two random circles' positions. This differs from the plain hex jitter because the rows buckle and the circles are exchanged. Use it for 30% of the starts.
backlog.title: Lattice-then-compress init using anisotropic squares

backlog.spec: Write a numpy-vectorised, batched gradient-descent-with-momentum penalty relaxation over 200 starts at once, with centers of shape (B,26,2) and radii as variables, using the penalty sum(r) - mu*overlap^2. Anneal mu upwards. Rank the starts by the LP sum, then run full SLSQP on the top 15 only. Do this in a loop for the first 100s.
backlog.title: Batch evaluate with vectorised penalty relaxation of 200 starts

backlog.spec: Build the best packing, apply a random one of the 8 square symmetries, and remove 3 to 5 circles chosen at random, with a preference for the smallest. Re-insert them at the largest-clearance points found on a grid, and polish with SLSQP. Because the removed circles are chosen at random this explores different neighbourhoods. Run for about 80s.
backlog.title: Reflection/rotation-augmented restarts of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Change the rng seed in optimized_packing from 12345 to 777 and extend the time loop to 200 seconds (still finishing under 4 minutes including the final LP). Keep everything else unchanged. Purpose: check whether the -2.6360 basin is seed-dependent and sample new basins.
backlog.title: Replicate with different seed and full 200s budget

backlog.spec: Create 4 default_rng streams (seeds 1,2,3,4) and round-robin them for the start generator, tracking the best sum overall. Use the same initialiser mix. Run until 170s. This diversifies the sampling without changing the per-start cost.
backlog.title: Interleaved multi-seed restarts with per-seed streams

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best centers and radii, identify active constraints (slack < 1e-7), and solve the KKT system of the fixed contact graph with Newton iterations via np.linalg.lstsq on variables (x,y,r) and the equalities for active pairs and walls. Accept only if the LP radii sum on the result is higher. Then keep the 1e-10 shrink.
backlog.title: Trust-constr/active-set KKT polish of the final best

backlog.spec: After a 110s multistart, take the best centers, apply a random one of the 8 square symmetries, then perturb 3 random circles by sigma 0.05 and re-polish with SLSQP. Repeat for 60s. Since symmetries leave the optimum invariant, the perturbation explores different neighbours of the same basin with varied SLSQP trajectories.
backlog.title: Reflection/rotation augmented restarts of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In _polish, run SLSQP first on the objective -(sum r^p)^(1/p) with p=0.5 (concave, favours equalising radii), then p=0.8, then plain sum. Use the analytic gradient of the objective, maxiter 100 for each earlier stage and 300 for the last. Use this for 40% of starts.
backlog.title: p-norm continuation on radii objective

backlog.spec: Implement a batched numpy gradient descent on 200 starts at once with arrays of shape (200,26,2) and radii (200,26), minimising -sum r + mu*overlap^2 with mu annealed from 10 to 1e5 over 400 steps using Adam. Then SLSQP-polish only the 8 starts with best feasibilised LP sum. Run for ~60s of batches, then use the rest of the time on standard starts.
backlog.title: Vectorised penalty relaxation of 200 starts

backlog.spec: Initialise with large circles (r~0.13) on a staggered 4-wide pattern in the interior, medium circles along edges and small circles (r~0.07) in the corners and gaps. Choose the counts randomly summing to 26 (e.g. 6 large, 12 medium, 8 small), place them by greedy Poisson-disk with class radii and passing radii as SLSQP start values. Use for 30% of starts.
backlog.title: Cluster-based three-radius-class lattice init

backlog.spec: Generate a hex lattice with spacing s in [0.16,0.21], rotate by a random angle, and scale the x and y axes by independent factors in [0.85,1.15] before clipping to the square. Keep the 26 points nearest to the center after random offset, add small jitter, and use for 30% of starts.
backlog.title: Lattice-compress init with anisotropic squeeze

backlog.spec: After a 110s multistart, repeat for 60s: choose a random disc of radius 0.3 in the unit square, fix all circles outside it (centers and radii as lower bounds only), re-randomise the centers of circles inside with uniform samples in the disc, and run SLSQP over all variables. Accept if the sum improves.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood re-solve of a sub-region

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 1e-10 shrink: compute the max violation in double precision for pairs (dist - ri - rj) and walls, and subtract just enough from the offending radii (max violation + 1e-15), looping until zero violations. Verify strictly with np.hypot and the harness conditions. This gains ~1e-9 and guards validity.
backlog.title: Robust final feasibility with minimal shrink

backlog.spec: Make no edit to train.py (or only a comment change) and rerun to confirm the -2.6360 result is repeatable with the fixed seed 12345. This checks run-to-run variation before further bold changes. The wall-clock time limit on the multi-start loop makes the number of starts vary, so also record the result.
backlog.title: Replicate run unchanged

backlog.spec: After a 110s multi-start, take the best packing. Generate its 8 dihedral images (reflections and rotations of centers about 0.5). For each image apply a small Gaussian jitter (sigma 0.01) to centers, run _polish and _lp_radii, and keep the best. Also try jitter combined with swapping the positions of two random similar-sized circles. Use the remaining ~40s for this.
backlog.title: Incumbent-only symmetry-augmented restarts

backlog.spec: Add a batched stage in numpy: hold 200 random-center, random-radius states as arrays of shape (200,26,2) and (200,26). Run 300 steps of Adam on a quadratic overlap and wall penalty with the penalty weight annealed upward and radii growing. Rank the starts by LP radii sum, and send only the top 8 to _polish. Run this for the first 60s, then continue with the existing loop for the rest.
backlog.title: Vectorised numpy penalty relaxation of 200 starts

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that builds a lattice-like layout with three circle classes. The classes are 4 large corner circles (r about 0.14), about 12 medium edge circles (r about 0.1) and about 10 small interior circles (r about 0.09). Place the circles by sequential random placement with rejection at those target radii, using jitter. Pass the centers into _polish. Use it for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Three-radius-class cluster lattice init

backlog.spec: Create a regular triangular lattice that has about 30 points in a rectangle with random aspect ratio between 0.8 and 1.25. Rotate it by a random angle. Rescale it non-uniformly to fit the unit square, then delete the 4 points with the least clearance to the walls. Add jitter and polish. Use it for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Anisotropic compress lattice init

backlog.spec: In _polish, run SLSQP first on the objective minimise sum r^0.7 combined with the sum-of-radii constraints unchanged. Then run it on the plain sum r objective, warm started. This smooths the landscape and favours balanced radii. Apply it to half of the starts as a different basin selector, keeping the existing single-stage polish for the other half.
backlog.title: p-norm continuation on radii objective

backlog.spec: After a 100s multi-start, repeat for ~70s. Choose a random disk of radius 0.3 in the unit square. Take the circles whose centers lie inside it (typically 5 to 9) and re-randomise their centers inside the disk. Keep the other circles fixed, then run a full _polish on all circles and accept if the LP sum improves. Choose the disk center preferentially near circles with fewer contacts.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood sub-region re-solve

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, run scipy minimize with method trust-constr on the best packing. Use the same variables and constraints, the analytic Jacobian and a tight gtol of 1e-12. Take the LP radii on the result and accept it only if the sum increases. Cap this stage at 30s.
backlog.title: Trust-constr KKT polish of the final best

backlog.spec: Replace the single rng with four rngs seeded 12345, 1, 2 and 3 and cycle through them per start. Each stream uses its own initialiser mix. Keep the global best. This diversifies against a lucky seed and keeps the same 150s budget.
backlog.title: Interleaved multi-seed round robin

backlog.spec: Place 28 circles by Lloyd relaxation on the grid and run a quick SLSQP polish on 28 circles. Then drop the 2 circles with the smallest radii, or the 2 circles with the lowest contact count. Re-polish the remaining 26. Use it for 20% of starts, replacing the old 27/28 attempts with this variant that includes the contact-count criterion.
backlog.title: Pair-exclusion density-aware init with removal from 28

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py except keeping the current seed 12345 and the 150s loop. This checks that the incumbent -2.6360 is repeatable and valid under the zero-tolerance checker. Use it as a baseline for the other ideas.
backlog.title: Replicate run unchanged

backlog.spec: In _polish, run SLSQP first on the objective -sum(r^p) with p=0.5 (this favours equal radii and spreads circles out), then p=0.75, then p=1. Warm-start each stage from the previous one with maxiter 100. Apply this to the best 30% of starts, ranked by their LP sum after a plain polish. Keep the plain-polish result if it is better.
backlog.title: p-norm radii objective continuation

backlog.spec: Add a batch pre-stage in numpy. Hold 200 random starts as an array (200,26,3) of x, y, r. Run 300 steps of projected gradient or Adam on the overlap penalty plus wall penalty minus the radius sum, with the penalty weight annealed upward. Then rank the starts by LP sum and run full SLSQP only on the top 15. Spend about 20s on this pre-stage, then the old loop for the remainder.
backlog.title: Vectorised penalty relaxation of 200 starts

backlog.spec: After a 100s multi-start, take the best packing and apply random dihedral symmetries (the 8 square symmetries). Add jitter with sigma 0.02 to the centres, and multiply each radius by lognormal(0, 0.15). Then re-polish with SLSQP. The kicks must be random and large enough to change the contact topology. Run this for about 60s and keep the best result.
backlog.title: Reflection-augmented incumbent restarts

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser with 4 corner circles of radius about 0.12, 12 edge circles of radius about 0.10, and 10 interior circles of radius about 0.11. Place them by random sequential insertion with rejection, using those target radii as the exclusion distances (sum of radii). Then run a short Lloyd-style repulsion and the usual SLSQP polish. Use it for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Three-radius-class cluster init

backlog.spec: Take the final best packing. Compute its active contact set (slack < 1e-7). Solve the KKT linear system for the sum-of-radii LP-like problem restricted to active constraints by Newton iterations. Alternatively, run scipy trust-constr with a tight gtol on the same variables and analytic Jacobian. Accept the result only if the sum rises and an exact double-precision feasibility check passes.
backlog.title: Trust-constr KKT polish of the best

backlog.spec: Generate an initial hexagonal lattice with spacing 0.17 to 0.2 in a rectangle of random aspect (0.8 to 1.2 wide, 0.8 to 1.2 tall) that is larger than the unit square. Randomly rotate it by 0 to 30 degrees and delete points outside it until 26 remain (keep the points nearest the centre). Then affinely squeeze it into the unit square with a margin of 0.05 before SLSQP. Use it for 30% of starts.
backlog.title: Anisotropic compress lattice init

backlog.spec: Replace the single rng with 6 independent generators (seeds 12345, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5). Rotate through them per start so that every stream samples all initialiser types. Track the best result per stream. At the end return the global best.
backlog.title: Interleaved multi-seed round robin

backlog.spec: For each start, set a random weight vector w with w_i uniform in [0.5,1.5]. Run an SLSQP stage with 60 iterations maximising sum(w_i r_i). Then do a second stage with the weights blended linearly to 1 over three sub-stages (60 iterations each). Run this for 40% of starts, with the others using the plain polish.
backlog.title: Random radius-target polish with sum-of-radii homotopy

backlog.spec: Change only the rng seed in optimized_packing from 12345 to 2024 and keep the 150s loop. This checks whether -2.6360 is reproducible across seeds or a lucky basin. Log nothing else; the result tells us the basin's robustness.
backlog.title: Unchanged replicate with different seed

backlog.spec: Record the best packing's sorted radii vector. For later starts, add a quadratic penalty to the SLSQP objective, in a first short stage only, that repels the sorted radii vector from this recorded one (weight 0.05*||sort(r)-r_best||^-1 style). Then run the plain final SLSQP polish with no penalty. This forces exploration of topologies different from the incumbent. Use it for 50% of starts in the second half of the time budget.
backlog.title: Incumbent-basin penalty restarts with distance tabu

backlog.spec: Build initial centres from a 3-class layout: 4 corner circles (large, r~0.13), about 12 edge circles (medium, r~0.1), and 10 interior circles (r~0.11) placed by Lloyd relaxation of a power diagram restricted to the interior. Pass these radii as the SLSQP initial r. Use it for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Contact-count-targeted lattice with 3 radius classes

backlog.spec: Use numpy to relax 300 random starts simultaneously as an array of shape (300,26,2) with a soft overlap and wall penalty, with gradient descent plus momentum and growing radii for 300 steps. Take the 15 with the highest sum of LP radii and polish them with SLSQP. This replaces about half of the time budget and gives much broader coverage of topologies per second.
backlog.title: Vectorised batch penalty relaxation of 300 starts

backlog.spec: Reparametrise the polish with variables X, Y and log-free radii r = s*r_scale, plus a trust-region bound of the centres around the starting values of 0.08 in a first stage, then release the bounds. Run this two-stage trust-box SLSQP in all starts. Bounded steps stop SLSQP from jumping between topologies early and may reach better local optima.
backlog.title: Radius-sorted constraint-ordering SLSQP reformulation

backlog.spec: Take the best packing, split circles into horizontal bands by y (3 to 5 bands at random cuts), shift one band horizontally by a random amount in 0.02 to 0.1 (wrapping to stay in the square by clipping), and re-polish with SLSQP. Repeat in the last 60s with the multi-start shortened to 90s. This is a structural move on rows that point perturbations cannot make.
backlog.title: Cyclic shift of strips in the incumbent

backlog.spec: Polish with the objective (sum r - T)^2 style replaced by a smooth concave surrogate: maximise sum sqrt(r+eps) for 60 iterations, then sum r^0.8, then sum r. This weights small circles more early and lets SLSQP rebalance sizes before the linear objective is applied. Use it on a random 40% of starts.
backlog.title: Annealed target-sum objective

backlog.spec: Place the 4 corner circles and k=10 to 12 circles along the walls at random spacing, solve LP radii, then place the remaining 10 to 12 interior circles by greedy max-clearance insertion with the boundary circle radii fixed. Then run the full SLSQP polish. Use it for 25% of starts with random k and random wall spacing.
backlog.title: Boundary-first construction with interior LP

backlog.spec: Generate initial centres from a square lattice rotated by 45 degrees (a checkerboard of spacing 0.19 to 0.23 with random offset), keep the points inside [0.04,0.96], then add or delete random points to get 26. Then polish. Use it for 20% of starts. This covers diagonal lattice topologies that the row-based initialisers do not.
backlog.title: Rotated-frame lattice with 45-degree orientation

backlog.spec: For each start, draw a random ratio q in 1.3 to 2.2 and give a random 8 to 14 circles radius q times the radius of the rest, scaled so the total area is about 0.78. Place them by greedy dart-throwing largest-first, then run SLSQP with these radii as the initial values. This bimodal start is aimed at packings with a few big circles and many small ones, as the known best structure seems to be.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class fixed-ratio restart

backlog.spec: Keep optimized_packing as is but run the multi-start loop with two seeds sequentially (12345 for 75s, then 2024 for 75s), keeping the overall best by LP sum. This checks repeatability and whether the 2.6360 basin is the global one across seeds. Final radii shrink stays 1e-10.
backlog.title: Unchanged replicate, different seed list

backlog.spec: After the multi-start, take the best centers and radii and run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' using the same squared-distance constraints (NonlinearConstraint with analytic jacobian, sparse not needed), xtol=1e-14, gtol=1e-12, maxiter 500. Accept the result only if the LP radii sum on its centers exceeds the current best. Limit to 30s.
backlog.title: Trust-constr KKT polish of final best

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 1e-10 shrink by an exact double-precision repair. After the final LP, compute for each pair the violation dist - (ri+rj) and each wall violation. Where negative, reduce the two radii by half the violation plus 1e-16. Then verify with np.hypot and a strict check, and apply a shrink of 1e-14 only if a violation remains. This recovers about 2e-9 and is safe.
backlog.title: Exact-margin final radius fix-up

backlog.spec: For the best packing, identify active constraints (slack<1e-9) among pair and wall constraints. Solve the square or least-squares system slack=0 in variables x,y,r with Newton and lstsq, starting from the SLSQP solution, to get machine-precision contacts. Then run the LP on the new centers and keep it if the sum is larger. This squeezes out the last 1e-9.
backlog.title: Fixed-contact-graph Newton solve

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that picks counts for big (r~0.13), medium (r~0.10) and small (r~0.07) circles such as 4/10/12, places the bigs near corners and centre, mediums along edges and smalls in gaps via random-order Poisson-disk sampling with these target radii, then passes them as the SLSQP start. Use for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Three-radius-class cluster lattice init

backlog.spec: Run a batched numpy Adam on a (300,26,3) array of x,y,r with penalty for overlap and walls and annealed mu from 10 to 1e5 plus a reward on sum r, for 800 steps. Rank the starts by feasible-LP sum, then SLSQP-polish the top 15 only. This uses 40s to screen far more starts than SLSQP can.
backlog.title: Vectorised numpy penalty relaxation of 300 starts

backlog.spec: Before the plain SLSQP, run a 100-iteration SLSQP maximising sum r minus lam*sum((r - r_target)^2), where r_target is drawn per start from lognormal(0,0.3) scaled to a mean of 0.1, and lam decays 1, 0.3, 0 over three stages. The target radius diversity pushes SLSQP into different contact topologies. Use for half the starts.
backlog.title: Radius-ratio target regularised polish

backlog.spec: After a 110s multi-start, spend 40s on restarts from the best packing. Cut it at a random vertical or horizontal line, mirror or cyclically shift one strip by a small amount (0.02-0.1), jitter all centers by 0.01, and full SLSQP polish. Keep the best.
backlog.title: Reflection-augmented incumbent restarts with strip shifts

backlog.spec: Place 12-14 circles around the perimeter, each tangent to a wall (corners tangent to two walls) with random spacing and radii from a sorted Dirichlet split. Fill the interior with the remaining circles by Lloyd on the free area, then do SLSQP polish. Use for 30% of starts to explore edge-dominated topologies.
backlog.title: Boundary-first construction with interior LP

backlog.spec: Leave train.py logic as is, but change only the rng seed in optimized_packing from 12345 to 2024 and keep the 150s budget. This checks whether -2.6360 is a robust basin or a seed artifact, and gives a replicate measurement of the incumbent.
backlog.title: Replicate unchanged run with new seed

backlog.spec: After the multi-start (shortened to 120s), take the best packing and identify active contacts (pair slack<1e-7, wall slack<1e-7). Solve the square nonlinear system for those contacts with scipy.optimize.root (method 'lm') over x,y,r, using only contacts for rigid-core circles. Accept only if the LP-verified sum improves. Then shrink radii by 1e-12 and verify pairs in double precision.
backlog.title: Fixed-contact-graph Newton on incumbent with exact KKT

backlog.spec: Initialise by choosing k in 4..10 large circles (radius ratio 1.3-2 to the others) with sum of areas filling about 0.8. Place them via random sequential insertion with exclusion, then place the remaining circles by Lloyd relaxation with the large circles frozen. Polish with SLSQP at free radii. Use for 30% of starts.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class fixed-ratio restart

backlog.spec: Generate a square lattice rotated by a random angle (biased to 45 degrees and 0), with spacing chosen so about 28-34 points fall in the square. Pick 26 points by dropping the ones closest to the boundary at random, compress them toward the center by a radial warp, jitter by 0.01, and polish with the existing SLSQP+LP. Use for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Rotated 45-degree frame lattice init

backlog.spec: Run 4 independent RNG streams in round-robin for the first 90s, tracking per-stream best. Then spend the remaining time only on the stream with the best result, using stronger jitter in its inits. This adds diversity without a change to the polish code.
backlog.title: Interleaved multi-seed round robin with best-seed focus

backlog.spec: Write a numpy routine that runs Adam on 300 random configurations at once, as a (300,26,3) array, with a penalty energy for overlap and wall violation and an annealed mu. Use per-circle sum-of-radii as the reward. Rank by feasible LP sum after the relaxation. Send the top 20 to SLSQP polish. Use about 40s for the batch and the rest for normal multi-start.
backlog.title: Vectorised batch penalty relaxation of 300 starts

backlog.spec: After a 100s multi-start, repeat for 60s: choose a random disc region of radius 0.25 in the best packing. Re-randomise the circles inside it (uniform in the region), keep the others fixed for the first SLSQP pass with maxiter 60, then free all circles for a full polish. Accept if the sum improves.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood sub-region re-solve

backlog.spec: After the multi-start (120s), run scipy minimize with method trust-constr on the best packing using the squared-distance constraints and the analytic Jacobians, with gtol 1e-12 and 400 iterations. Replace the packing only if the LP sum on its centers is higher. Then use the existing margin shrink.
backlog.title: Trust-constr KKT polish of final best

backlog.spec: In _polish, run SLSQP first on -sum(r^0.7) for 100 iterations. This favours equalising radii and shifts the basin. Then run the original -sum(r) objective for the full 300 iterations. Apply to 50% of starts, selected at random per start.
backlog.title: Radius p-norm continuation objective

backlog.spec: Place 12-16 circles along the perimeter at an inset equal to the target radius, with random per-circle radii in 0.07-0.12 and spacing from neighbour contact. Fill the interior with Lloyd relaxation for the remaining circles and then polish with SLSQP and LP. Use for 25% of starts and vary the perimeter count.
backlog.title: Boundary-first construction with interior LP

backlog.spec: Make no functional change to train.py except keeping the seed at 12345 and the 150s loop. Run once more to confirm that the -2.6360 result is repeatable. If the result differs, the time-based loop is the cause, so replace the wall-clock loop with a fixed iteration count calibrated to about 150s.
backlog.title: Replicate run unchanged to check repeatability

backlog.spec: Replace the time-based while loop in optimized_packing with a fixed number of starts (for example 400, and break out early if time exceeds 220s as a safety net). The result then does not depend on machine speed. Keep the initialiser mix and the seed unchanged.
backlog.title: Fixed iteration-count multistart for determinism

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing and run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same [x,y,r] variables. Use the analytic Jacobian, a NonlinearConstraint with lower bound 0 and tolerances of 1e-12. Then compute the LP radii on the resulting centers. Accept the result only if the LP sum is higher than the current best. Cap this step at 40s.
backlog.title: Trust-constr KKT polish of the final best

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that builds a square lattice rotated by 45 degrees (a diamond lattice) with a random spacing between 0.17 and 0.22 and a random offset. Keep the points that fall inside [0.04, 0.96]^2. Randomly add or delete points to reach 26, add jitter of 0.01, and use it for 20% of the starts.
backlog.title: Rotated 45-degree frame lattice init

backlog.spec: Place about 12 to 16 circles around the boundary, at the corners and evenly spaced along the edges with random phase. Fill the interior with 10 to 14 points chosen by a Lloyd relaxation that excludes the boundary circles. Then run the existing LP and SLSQP. Use it for 25% of the starts.
backlog.title: Boundary-first construction with interior LP

backlog.spec: Run a numpy batch of 300 starts at once with shape (300,26,3), holding x, y and r. Use annealed quadratic-penalty gradient descent with momentum for 500 steps and increase mu over the steps. Take the 15 starts with the highest feasible radius sum and run SLSQP on each. Merge these with the normal multistart as an extra source of starts.
backlog.title: Vectorised penalty relaxation of 300 starts

backlog.spec: In _polish, add a first SLSQP stage of 80 iterations. The objective is sum r - lam * sum((r - t)^2), where t is a random lognormal(0, 0.3) target vector scaled to sum to 2.63 and lam = 0.5. Then run the plain sum r objective. Use this on 40% of the starts.
backlog.title: Random-radius-target regularised polish

backlog.spec: After a 100s multistart, take the best packing and generate variants. Each variant applies a random choice of reflection or transpose, followed by a cyclic shift of one random horizontal or vertical strip by 0.05 to 0.15. Add jitter of 0.01 and re-polish with SLSQP. Accept the result only if it improves. Run this for 60s.
backlog.title: Reflection and strip-shift augmented incumbent restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the 1e-10 shrink with an LP re-solve on the best centres. Then loop: compute the worst double-precision violation of any pair or wall, and scale the offending radii by 1 - 2*violation. Repeat until there are no violations. This keeps the shrink minimal, close to 1e-15 instead of 1e-10 per circle.
backlog.title: Exact-margin radius fix-up

backlog.spec: Make no change to train.py except nothing functional: keep the 150s seeded multi-start as is, to confirm the -2.6360 result is repeatable and the final validity check passes. Only add a harmless comment line at the top of the evolve block.
backlog.title: Replicate unchanged for repeatability

backlog.spec: Change the multi-start loop limit from 150s to 215s, and also check time before each start so no start begins after 215s. Keep the seed 12345 stream so earlier starts are identical and extra starts only add candidates. Leave the 1e-10 radius shrink.
backlog.title: Time-budget extension to 220s with early-time guard

backlog.spec: After the multi-start (shorten to 110s), take the best packing. For 60s repeat: pick a random circle, delete it, run SLSQP on the other 25 for a few iterations, then reinsert it at a random point in the largest empty disk (grid of 60x60 with distance-to-circles clearance), and run the full SLSQP polish with the 26-circle problem. Accept only if the sum improves. Use fresh random choices each trial among the 8 smallest-radius circles.
backlog.title: Basin-hop in the active-contact subspace with stochastic radius LP

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that assigns 10-14 circles a big radius R and the rest a small radius r with R/r random in 1.3-2.2, places big circles by Poisson-disk sampling first and then small ones in the remaining gaps (dart throwing with the true radii, relaxing the sizes by 0.97 if stuck), and pass these centers into the existing LP then SLSQP polish. Use for 25% of starts.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class fixed ratio start

backlog.spec: After the multi-start (shorten to 120s), run scipy trust-constr on the best (x,y,r) vector with the same squared-distance constraints and analytic Jacobian, gtol 1e-12, maxiter 500. Accept only if the LP-radii sum on the resulting centers is larger.
backlog.title: Trust-constr KKT polish of final best

backlog.spec: After a 100s multi-start, for 60s generate perturbations of the best packing: reflect or rotate it, then shift a random horizontal or vertical band of circles by a random amount of up to 0.5 of a circle diameter and add noise of 0.01 to all centres. Polish with SLSQP and keep the best.
backlog.title: Reflection and strip-shift restarts of incumbent

backlog.spec: In _polish for half the starts, first run 100 SLSQP iterations on the objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-t)^2), where t is random lognormal(0,0.4) targets scaled to sum 2.6 and lam=0.5. Then run the normal polish from that result. This varies the basin reached.
backlog.title: Random radius-target regularised polish

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 1e-10 shrink. Compute double-precision violations for every pair (r_i+r_j-d) and wall (r-x etc.). Subtract the max violation per circle from both circles involved, iterating until none is positive, then subtract 1e-15. The aim is to gain about 1e-10 and ensure that the result stays valid.
backlog.title: Exact feasibility repair then minimal shrink

backlog.spec: Leave the algorithm unchanged but change the rng seed in optimized_packing from 12345 to 20240607 and keep the 150s loop. This measures repeatability and seed variance of the current -2.6360 basin. Only the seed line changes.
backlog.title: Unchanged replicate, different seed

backlog.spec: After the multi-start (shorten it to 135s), take the best packing and identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-9). Solve the KKT system of the active set for the stationary point with a few Newton steps using lstsq on [x,y,r] and multipliers from the LP dual. Accept only if the LP-recomputed sum improves. Then finish with the usual 1e-10 shrink.
backlog.title: Fixed contact-graph Newton on incumbent

backlog.spec: Shorten the multi-start to 100s. Then for 50s generate starts from the best packing by applying a random dihedral symmetry, then shifting one random horizontal or vertical band (centers with y in a random interval) by a random offset of up to 0.08 in x, wrapping and clipping. Re-polish each with SLSQP and the LP, and keep the best.
backlog.title: Strip-shift and reflection incumbent restarts

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that picks k (4 to 10) circles as big with radius ratio rho uniform in 1.3 to 2.2 times the small ones. Run a short SLSQP maximising only a common scale s with fixed r_i = s*ratio_i, from random centers. Then release the radii in the full _polish. Use it for 30% of starts.
backlog.title: Two-radius-class fixed-ratio start

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 distinct results of a 120s multi-start. Polish each with scipy trust-constr using the analytic constraint Jacobian and a tight gtol of 1e-12, using NonlinearConstraint with the squared-distance formulation. Then run the LP on the centers and return the best.
backlog.title: Trust-constr KKT polish of top candidates

incumbent.description: Add a random hex-lattice generator (random rows/orientation/spacing/shift, random deletions or additions, jitter 0.005) used for 30% of starts.

memo:
Helped: seeded multi-start repulsion plus SLSQP polish (slot 0, -2.6343), then better initialisers: Lloyd on a dense grid (slot 2, -2.6359) and jittered hex rows (slot 8, -2.6360, incumbent). That beats the 2.635 target.

Did not help: population evolution (slot 1, -2.6317), staged radii-power objectives, corner-anchored and edge-ring inits (-2.6353), 5x5 grid init (-2.6343), power-diagram Lloyd, symmetric parametrisation. Re-polish, Newton, barrier, basin-hopping, differential evolution, iterated local search, screening, swap moves and margin-shrink variants all stayed at -2.6360. Since slot 8 nearly every slot has been flat (about 140 slots), so the basin looks saturated. Slots 3 and 8 each aborted once.

Next: run one replicate to check repeatability. Then try only a genuinely different topology or search objective, not more polish, screening, init or margin variants. Propose real edits, not no-op changes.
